Broker 0.01% Idle Cash Sweep vs SGOV Treasury Buffer for Age 55+ Retirees

Open your IRA statement tonight and look at the tiny line labeled 'core cash sweep.' On many major brokerages, default uninvested cash still earns roughly 0.01%—just $10 a year on $100,000.

Retirees hold cash for a noble reason: protecting sleep and avoiding forced stock sales during a downturn. Yet leaving two full years of retirement expenses sitting in a 0.01% bank sweep quietly bleeds purchasing power to groceries, property taxes, and Medicare premiums every single month.

That is why our 2000–2025 Retirement Study models a dedicated 24-month ultra-short U.S. Treasury bill buffer (SGOV, 0–3 month T-bills) alongside the SMH x XLV core. Because short-term T-bills carry minimal duration risk compared to 20-year bond funds, retirees keep daily liquidity while letting their safety bucket actually pull its weight.
